sections.name: Outreach & Engagement
sections.body:
We will use a family-centered outreach and intake approach tied to the population named in the proposal. "The proposed project aims to serve 60 Miami-Dade County children." (proposed_project_plan; TP-G01-PLAN-REACH) "The proposed project would serve children in elementary and middle school and engage their caregivers." (proposed_project_plan; TP-G01-PLAN-PARTICIPANTS) "Tidepath supports children and families through mentoring, family counseling, and school-based safety and mental-health workshops." (verified_organizational_fact; TF-001)

How children and caregivers will learn about and enter the program: the evidence does not specify outreach channels or enrollment steps. Tentatively, in time order we would: 1) coordinate with elementary and middle schools for referrals and information distribution; 2) conduct direct caregiver outreach by phone/email and at family events; 3) complete a brief intake call or school referral to enroll families. These steps are proposed and tentative.

How caregivers will participate and how barriers will be addressed: Tidepath's existing "family counseling" and "school-based safety and mental-health workshops" could be used to engage caregivers (verified_organizational_fact; TF-001). Proposed, tentative supports to reduce barriers include flexible scheduling, virtual participation options, and onsite or subsidized childcare and transportation assistance; these supports are tentative and subject to planning.

sections.name: Advancing Equity
sections.body: Tidepath supports children and families through mentoring, family counseling, and school-based safety and mental-health workshops. To advance equitable access, the design will tentatively address transportation, cost, scheduling, and language barriers that often limit family participation. Which access barriers does the design address? It will tentatively prioritize transportation, cost, scheduling, and language access. What concrete steps will reduce those barriers? In time order: first, conduct a brief needs assessment with partner schools and families to confirm priorities; next, pilot evening and weekend sessions and expand school-based delivery to reduce travel and scheduling burdens; then add bilingual outreach and translated materials to improve language access; simultaneously, offer sliding-scale or no-cost slots and transit stipends where feasible to reduce cost and transportation barriers; finally, evaluate outcomes and iterate with partner organizations. All proposed activities are tentative and subject to local needs and partner agreements and are proposed to serve Miami-Dade County children and caregivers.
